q: Autonomous codebase refactoring requires coding agents to restructure working software while strictly preserving externally observable behavior
r: EC6: performance-oriented refactoring benchmark; behaviour-preserving restructuring is neither feature/project development from requirements nor an evaluation-method contribution.

q: We call this a specification–oracle gap: where it exists, a benchmark also measures whether an agent reproduces upstream implementation details.
r: Include: audit method for milestone-level coding-agent benchmarks (spec vs test oracle), a contribution to evaluation method with 35 agent runs reanalysed.

q: Greenfield software development in freelance settings requires coding agents to turn incomplete client requests into working software.
r: Include: new benchmark of greenfield project development from incomplete requirements, nine models compared on implementation and clarification scores.

q: We introduce SWE-Shift, a benchmark for evaluating coding agents under such mid-execution changes.
r: Include: new evaluation design (matched Clean/Shifted continuations, token budget control) comparing 17 agent systems; contribution is the evaluation method.

q: retrospective empirical systems experience report follows my engineering work from July to October 2026 across coding clients, model-specific serving recipes, vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, and MLX.
r: Include: multi-trial controlled comparison of open-weight models vs direct frontier coding with hidden verification and cost per verified success; evaluation method and cost metrics.

q: We introduce FeatureLoop, a benchmark of 61 human-reviewed tasks from 34 repositories across five primary programming languages and seven software forms.
r: Include: feature-level iterative development under evolving requirements, 12 models on a shared harness, token cost and human-guidance metrics.

q: We distilled it from two manually configured industrial factories, observed for 15 and 17 days, and have not yet evaluated it.
r: EC3: short vision/position paper with plans and hypotheses, no completed controlled evaluation of coding agents.

q: Large language models are known to be sycophantic, over-complying with users even when doing so is unproductive.
r: EC6: observational-style behaviour study on repeated refactoring requests, not code development from requirements and not mainly an evaluation-method contribution.

q: Feature evolution requires evaluating successive extensions on an agent’s own earlier code and checking whether the feature remains correct.
r: Include: new benchmark of feature-level extension chains with requirement specifications and stage gates, new evaluation design for coding agents.

q: To succeed in real-world long-horizon software development, coding agents must satisfy multidimensional task specifications, such as interface compatibility and error handling, and do so without breaking existing dependencies.
r: EC5: main contribution is a task-synthesis/RL training method tested on existing SWE benchmarks (issue-repair style), adding little to evaluation method.
